Thought: Let me evaluate each option about methanol:

A. Its vapors are harmful - Methanol vapors are indeed toxic when inhaled. Methanol is known to be toxic to humans, causing potential blindness and even death when ingested, and its vapors can cause similar harmful effects.

B. Methanol can be used as a substitute for ethanol without any problems - This is false. Methanol is highly toxic compared to ethanol. Substituting methanol for ethanol (especially in alcoholic beverages) is extremely dangerous and can lead to blindness or death.

C. Methanol fires can be extinguished with water - This is true. Methanol is water-soluble, and water can be used to dilute and extinguish methanol fires, unlike many other alcohol fires that may require special extinguishing agents.

D. Skin contact is not harmful - This is false. Methanol can be absorbed through the skin, potentially causing toxicity. While brief contact may not cause immediate severe effects, prolonged or repeated skin exposure can lead to absorption and systemic toxicity.

Based on my analysis, statements A and C appear to be true.
